newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: LUGE-HACKL MAKES HISTORY WITH THIRD WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: LUGE-HACKL MAKES HISTORY WITH THIRD WORLD TITLE.

text.p: German veteran Georg Hackl became the first triple world champion in the history of men's luge competition when he clinched gold on Sunday with a superb fastest second-run time.
Hackl, 1988 and 1990 world champion, performed a near-perfect second run to improve on a first leg second place for overall victory in one minute 38.277 seconds.
The 30-year-old German, who also took gold at the 1992 and 1994 Olympics, had to undergo surgery after fracturing ribs last October and therefore surprised even himself with the win.
"I'm totally surprised, luck was obviously on my side today. I came here expecting to give an average performance only," said Hackl. "Now I have to sit down, I still can't stand for too long."
Austria's 1987 and 1996 world champion Markus Prock, who led after the first run, had to settle for silver (1:38.513) on an overcast day.
Prock also had to bow to Hackl at the last two Olympics.
"At the Olympics it was always very close. However, today I was quite a way behind Hackl," said Prock. "But I'm happy, silver also shines nicely."
Bronze on the course which staged the luge events of the 1964 and 1976 Innsbruck Olympic Games went to another Austrian, Gerhard Gleirscher (1:38.591).

Hackl's triumph was Germany's second gold medal at the 32nd edition of the world championships after Susi Erdmann's victory over compatriot and defending title-holder Jana Bode in the women's competition.
Erdmann's win also marked her third world championships title after 1989 and 1991.
The Germans also took silver in the team event on Friday, as well as silver and bronze in Saturday's doubles to become the most successful nation at the three-day championships.
Hosts Austria were second in the medal standings with two golds -- in the team event and doubles -- Prock's silver and two bronzes through Gleirscher and Angelika Neuner.
The only other country to take a medal was Italy, with bronze in the team competition.
